title: Set 73

sentences.ko: 우리 팀에 메일 보낼 때마다 팀장을 참조에 넣는 사람이 있어. 잠깐 시간 되냐고 묻는 메일까지도 그래. 그래서 그 얘기를 꺼냈더니 자기는 그렇게 해야 일이 정리된다는 거야. 그러니까 이제 괜히 유난 떠는 사람은 나야. 요즘은 메일 하나 보내는 데 네 번씩 고쳐 쓰고 있어. 이런 사람 되기 싫은데 이미 이렇게 됐네.
sentences.text: There's a guy on my team who copies my manager on every email, even when he's just asking if I've got two minutes. So I brought it up with him and he said that's just how he keeps track, and now I'm the one making it weird. I've been rewriting stuff four times before I send it, and I don't want to be that person, but here we are.

alts.text: This guy on my team cc's my manager on every single email, even when he's just asking if I've got two minutes. So I said something to him and he goes that's just how he keeps track, and now I'm the weird one. I've been rewriting stuff four times before I hit send, and I don't wanna be that person, but here we are.

There is a colleague on my team who copies my manager on every email, even when he is simply asking whether I have two minutes. I raised it with him and he said that is how he keeps track, and now I am the one who looks like I am making an issue of it. I have been rewriting messages four times before sending them, and I would prefer not to be that person, but that is where I am.

sentences.note: **copies my manager on every email** 은 모든 메일에 상사를 참조로 넣는다는 뜻이고, **making it weird** 는 별일 아닌 것을 괜히 이상한 일로 만든다는 말이에요. **but here we are** 는 원하지 않았지만 결국 이 꼴이 됐다는 체념 표현입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 왼쪽 앞 화구가 2주쯤 전부터 불이 안 붙어서 전화드려야지 하다가 계속 미뤘는데요, 이제 오븐까지 그래요. 화구 하나만 문제는 아닌 것 같아요. 그동안 전자레인지로만 때우고 있는데 집에 애가 둘이라 이것도 이제 슬슬 못 견디겠어요. 이번 주에 기사님 한 분 보내 주실 수 있을까요? 저는 화요일이랑 수요일에 집에 있어요.
sentences.text: Hey, the front left burner stopped lighting about two weeks ago and I kept meaning to call, but now the oven's doing it too, so I don't think it's just the one burner. We've been living off the microwave and that's getting old with two kids in the house. Any chance you can get somebody out this week? I'm home Tuesday and Wednesday.

alts.text: Quick one, that front left burner hasn't lit in like two weeks and I kept meaning to call, but now the oven's doing it too, so it's not just the one burner. We've been living off the microwave and that's getting old with two kids here. Any chance you could get somebody out this week? I'm home Tuesday and Wednesday.

Hello, the front left burner stopped lighting about two weeks ago and I kept meaning to call, but the oven is now doing the same, so I do not believe it is only the one burner. We have been living off the microwave, and that is wearing thin with two children in the house. Would it be possible to send someone out this week? I am home on Tuesday and Wednesday.

sentences.note: **kept meaning to call** 은 전화해야지 생각만 하고 계속 미뤘다는 뜻이에요. **living off the microwave** 는 전자레인지로만 끼니를 때운다는 말이고, **that's getting old** 는 이제 슬슬 지겹고 못 견디겠다는 표현입니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 데이나랑 파인가에 있는 그 카페에서 두 시에 만나기로 했는데, 가 보니까 자리마다 노트북 펴 놓고 한 시간 전에 다 마신 커피 한 잔 올려둔 사람들뿐이었어. 그래서 창가에 서서 누가 짐 챙겨 나가기를 기다렸는데, 십 분 있다가 그냥 포기하고 공원까지 걸어갔어. 밖은 엄청 추웠고. 다음엔 진짜 앉을 수 있는 데로 가자.
sentences.text: Dana and I were supposed to meet at that place on Pine at two, and when we got there every table had somebody with a laptop and one coffee they'd clearly finished an hour ago. So we stood by the window waiting for somebody to pack up, and after ten minutes we just gave up and walked to the park, and it was freezing out. Next time we're going somewhere you can actually sit down.

alts.text: Me and Dana were gonna meet at that place on Pine at two, and when we showed up every table had somebody with a laptop and one coffee they'd obviously finished an hour before. So we stood by the window waiting on somebody to pack up, and after ten minutes we just bailed and walked to the park, and it was freezing out. Next time we're going somewhere you can actually sit down.

Dana and I had arranged to meet at the place on Pine at two, and when we arrived every table was taken by someone with a laptop and a single coffee they had clearly finished an hour earlier. We waited by the window for someone to pack up, and after ten minutes we gave up and walked to the park, and it was freezing outside. Next time we will go somewhere we can actually sit down.

sentences.note: **pack up** 은 짐을 챙겨 자리를 뜬다는 뜻이고, **it was freezing out** 은 밖이 얼어붙게 추웠다는 구어 표현이에요. 캐주얼의 **bailed** 는 하던 것을 그만두고 그냥 빠져나왔다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 애가 다섯 시에 차에서 잠들었어. 이십 분, 딱 그게 다였는데 그것 때문에 밤이 통째로 망했어. 여덟 시에 옆에 같이 누웠는데 아홉 시 반까지도 계속 조잘대더라. 그러다 나도 잠들어서 열한 시에 애 방에서 불 켜 놓은 채로 깼어. 그래서 설거지는 아직 싱크대에 그대로고 나는 오늘 한 번도 앉아 보지를 못했어.
sentences.text: He fell asleep in the car at five, twenty minutes, that was it, and it wrecked the whole night. I laid down with him at eight and he was still talking at nine thirty, and then I fell asleep too and woke up in his room at eleven with the light on. So the dishes are still in the sink and I haven't sat down once today.

alts.text: Twenty minutes asleep in the car at five, that was it, and the whole night was shot. I got in bed with him at eight and he was still talking at nine thirty, then I passed out too and woke up in his room at eleven with the light on. So the dishes are still in the sink and I haven't sat down once today.

He fell asleep in the car at five for twenty minutes, no more than that, and it ruined the entire evening. I lay down with him at eight and he was still talking at nine thirty, and then I fell asleep as well and woke in his room at eleven with the light on. As a result the dishes are still in the sink and I have not sat down once today.

sentences.note: **wrecked the whole night** 은 그날 밤을 통째로 망쳤다는 뜻이에요. 캐주얼의 **the whole night was shot** 도 같은 뜻이고, **passed out** 은 곯아떨어졌다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 이모가 새 직장에서 실제로 얼마 받냐고 묻는 거야. 그것도 밥상에서 바로. 그러더니 사촌은 만나는 사람 있냐고 하고, 엄마는 그걸 그냥 다 보고만 있고. 그래서 나는 대충 얼버무리고 삼촌한테 배 얘기를 물었어. 삼촌은 그 배 얘기 시작하면 이십 분은 하거든. 그걸로 디저트 나올 때까지 다 버텼어.
sentences.text: My aunt asked what I'm actually making at the new job, right there at the table, and then my cousin wanted to know if I'm seeing anybody, and my mom just let the whole thing happen. So I kept it vague and asked my uncle about his boat, because he'll go on about that boat for twenty minutes, and that got me all the way through dessert.

alts.text: So my aunt goes and asks what I'm actually making at the new job, right there at the table, and then my cousin wants to know if I'm seeing anybody, and my mom just let the whole thing happen. So I kept it vague and got my uncle going about his boat, because he'll go on about that boat for twenty minutes, and that got me all the way through dessert.

My aunt asked what I am actually earning at the new job, right there at the table, and then my cousin wanted to know whether I am seeing anyone, and my mother simply allowed it all to happen. I kept my answer vague and asked my uncle about his boat, since he will go on about that boat for twenty minutes, and that carried me all the way through dessert.

sentences.note: **kept it vague** 은 구체적으로 답하지 않고 대충 얼버무렸다는 뜻이에요. **go on about** 은 한 가지 얘기를 지겹도록 늘어놓는다는 말이고, 캐주얼의 **got my uncle going** 은 상대가 신나서 떠들게 말을 붙였다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

reviewed: 1번 formal 의 "now I am the one who seems to be making it strange" 는 관용구(making it weird)를 글자대로 풀어 놓아 원어민이 쓰지 않는 말이 됐습니다. 뜻은 그대로 두고 "now I am the one who looks like I am making an issue of it" 으로 고쳤습니다.
2번 casual 이 text 와 거의 글자까지 같았습니다. 앞부분과 표현을 더 구어체로 바꿨습니다 (that front left burner hasn't lit in like two weeks / so it's not just the one burner / with two kids here). 노트가 짚는 표현 세 개는 그대로 남겼습니다.
3번 formal 의 "somewhere one can actually sit down" 은 자기 얘기를 하면서 one 을 쓴 것이라 지나치게 딱딱하고 어색합니다. "somewhere we can actually sit down" 으로 고쳤습니다.
